title: Usage/cost and notification contracts — completing the shared kernel

independence.cross_vendor_exception: Not satisfied: every assigned run is Anthropic claude-opus-5. The Decision Register permits a single-vendor fallback only as an explicit recorded exception. Five separate runs with distinct capability declarations, none reviewing its own work, is that fallback. It is not equivalent to cross-vendor review, and runs sharing a vendor and a model share a correlated blind spot.

required_human_authorities: Product Owner disposition of RFC-2026-004 before the manual merge described in RFC-2026-002
A1 security owner disposition of the CTR-MOD-001 / CTR-SEC-001 secret-handle syntax ownership conflict, and of the handle issuance format that CTR-SEC-001 cannot specify
purpose: Materialize the last two Draft shared-kernel contracts, CTR-USG-001 and CTR-NTF-001, completing all 14 entries in the Sprint 0A contract catalog. Written schema-first with every rule carrying an x-source, following the method that WP-0A-CON-003 and WP-0A-CON-004 established after WP-0A-CON-002 was rejected twice for letting schema and test predicates drift apart.

include: CTR-USG-001 schema, manifest and synthetic fixtures: OB-004's six usage dimensions, its attribution requirement, and decimal-string money
CTR-NTF-001 schema, manifest and synthetic fixtures: PT-007's command/result split, permission-checked deep link, ID-005 dedupe,
An x-source on every rule naming the baseline task, and a declared inference wherever a rule is derived rather than quoted
untestable_by_fixture and untestable_by_schema declarations for what neither can demonstrate
exclude: Contract freeze-level advancement, contract-catalog/shared-kernel/index.json, the provider price list, currency conversion, the OB-008 reconciliation algorithm, the OB-006 safe metric-label set, notification retry policy and dedupe window, email and LINE adapter shapes, the MOD-100 preference model, production schema, migrations, provider SDKs, credentials, customer data, network calls, Gate G0 approval and any merge authorization

contracts_produced: CTR-USG-001 and CTR-NTF-001 materialized at Draft only; no freeze-level advancement

ownership.forbidden_paths_note: The globs **/*secret* and **/*credential* were removed because six manifests declared them while shipping outputs that matched, and the ownership validator could not see the contradiction until it began comparing outputs against forbidden_paths. An earlier version of this note was copied verbatim from WP-0A-CON-004 and asserted that this package 'materializes the secret-handle contract itself', which is FALSE here -- CON-004 has 25 such outputs and this package has none. Independent review found the copied falsehood. Replaced with the extensions that carry real key material.

amends_without_owning.rationale:
This branch rewrites open_blockers in this package's own manifest and the handoff that cites them -- both owned outright. Two files outside that are touched and neither is optional. The branch-to-package mapping is pinned whole in test-kits/branch-identity.test.mjs, so declaring a new branch for this package moves one row there; the test asserts the mapping as a single object, which is exactly why the row cannot be added quietly. test-kits/integrity-manifest.json moves because branch-identity.test.mjs is a digested file and npm run regenerate:manifest recomputes its digest. No floor is lowered, no digested file leaves the protected set, and no test is added or removed.

The four prose entries previously in authorized_cross_package_amendments were removed. They were accurate for the increment merged in pull request #9 -- negative fixtures added to ctr-evt-001 and ctr-job-001, the two contract test suites amended, and the integrity manifest recomputed -- and they describe nothing this branch touches. Following the precedent WP-0A-DB-00 set on 2026-09-05: a declaration matching none of the diff is not a record, it is a standing permission over four paths that nobody reviewed for this branch, and verify-branch-scope.mjs honours both fields identically. The history they carried is in the merged commits, in evidence/WP-0A-CON-006/, and in this package's handoff.

acceptance_criteria: Every fixture is validated against its own shipped schema.json by the subset validator; both contracts passed conformance without a correction round.
Every rule carries an x-source naming the baseline task, and states whether it is quoted or a declared inference.
Money and quantity are decimal STRINGS, never numbers: Decision Register 4.2 MOD-130 forbids floating-point money.

A notification deep link requires a permission check as a const, and a delivery failure records that it did not roll back the domain result as a const -- both expressed in the contract rather than in prose.
All 14 shared-kernel contracts are now materialized; the index still reports 4 Candidate and 10 Draft, so materializing a Draft does not promote it.
npm run check passes on pinned Node 24.20.0 / npm 11.19.0 with skipped and todo both zero.
Every contract in the catalog reaches a per-contract mutation-coverage floor of 30%, computed rather than enumerated, so a contract added later by someone who never reads the guard is still measured.
The mutation-coverage metric counts assertion keywords only, so a schema cannot raise its score by deleting a rule or by adding a property that constrains nothing.

The coverage guard cannot be improved by deleting a rule: each contract declares both a floor on its constraint-site count and a ceiling on its unkilled sites, so removing a constraint lowers a number that must be edited deliberately.
required_tests: Schema conformance for both contracts via the subset validator
Negative cases: floating-point cost notation, missing provider attribution, an unknown usage dimension, a metric label carrying user content
Negative cases: a deep link without a permission check, a public-URL deep link, a failure without a class, a command carrying delivery state, free text where a message key is required
Repository protocol, ownership, role-separation and secret-scan checks
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR; removing the two contract directories leaves no persisted data, provider state, credential, migration or customer-data effect.
open_blockers: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-06, verified against the tree rather than remembered. This entry read: 'RFC-2026-004 is Proposed and requires Product Owner disposition before the RFC-2026-002 manual merge.' The Status line of architecture/decisions/RFC-2026-004-catalog-reference-integrity.md now reads 'Approved 2026-09-02 by the Product Owner -- the $ref integrity guard is live and no freeze level moved', so the disposition this entry was waiting for has happened. What remains is narrower and is that RFC's own Limitations section, which the approval leaves standing word for word: it does not approve Gate G0, does not authorize a merge, does not advance any contract freeze level, and does not substitute for the independent Reviewer, Tester, Security or Integration Owner evidence RFC-2026-002 requires. Every merge of this package still needs all of that separately; what it no longer needs is a disposition of RFC-2026-004.

CTR-NTF-001 SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN AUTHORED BY THIS PACKAGE. Independent review graded it High: Decision Register 4.1 reserves proposing a contract to its owner and 4.3 makes A0's role 'producer submits proposal and fixture; A0 assigns version'. A5 is the sole owner and A0 wrote the proposal. Ratification after the fact is a weaker and different control. The '14 of 14 materialized' figure therefore counts an unratified non-owner draft as coverage and must not be cited as G0 evidence without that qualification.

CTR-NTF-001 is owned by A5, not A0. It is materialized here from the baseline and REQUIRES A5 ratification before freeze. This is the same class of ownership irregularity that CTR-MOD-001 created for CTR-SEC-001, and it is recorded rather than resolved because A5 is not in this session.

A6 has not supplied an independently reviewed capability benchmark for billing-cost-ops (see WP-0A-A6-001), so the cost semantics here are materialized from the baseline and require A6 ratification.' And the ratification happened: evidence/WP-0A-CON-004/co-owner-review-sec-aud-obs-usg.md records 'Third A6 assessment of CTR-USG-001 -- 2026-09-02 -- SIGNED', after two refusals, with four blocking conditions closed in the same change. THREE NARROWER THINGS REMAIN. (a) The benchmark recommends WITH CONDITIONS and forward only, and its own C1 says no package may be staffed on it alone; the assessor shares a vendor and a model with the assessed run, so it is not vendor-independent. (b) A6's fifth condition is recorded rather than fixed: dedupe_key.minLength 1 is dead because the shortest pattern-satisfying key is 44 characters, and invalid-float-cost.json carries a basis value from a removed enum, so both fixtures fail for two reasons and neither witnesses the rule its filename names. (c) CTR-USG-001 still reads Draft in contract-catalog/shared-kernel/index.json. A co-owner signature is not a freeze-level advance, and RFC-2026-010 promoted five A0-owned contracts, not this one.

OB-008 reconciliation -- detecting missing and duplicate usage against a provider statement -- and ID-005 dedupe suppression are properties of a ledger or a store across many events. Declared in untestable_by_fixture and NOT claimed as materialized.

SUPERSEDED 2026-09-06, verified against the tree. This entry read: 'metric_labels is held at maxProperties 0 because OB-006's safe label set does not exist yet. An open object would invite an unsafe one; this is a deliberate placeholder, not a modelled rule.' There is no such placeholder any more. metric_labels was REMOVED from CTR-USG-001 outright; the schema contains neither the property nor the keyword maxProperties anywhere. The manifest's freeze_boundary records the reason independent review gave: Decision Register 5.2 assigns bounded label cardinality to the CTR-OBS-001 row and not to this one, CTR-OBS-001 already implements it in sli_tags, and carrying it here was the exact inverse of the 'right row, wrong column' error CTR-OBS-001 itself records. What remains is the part the placeholder was standing in for: OB-006's safe metric-label set still does not exist. It is now entirely CTR-OBS-001's problem, expressed in sli_tags, and this package neither owns that contract nor records the label hazard anywhere in its own.
That a cost figure is arithmetically correct for its quantity is declared in untestable_by_schema. Only OB-008 can check it.

PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-09-06, verified against the tree; the three claims this entry made are answered separately and only two of them are closed. It read: 'This package depends on five unmerged packages and inherits every open blocker recorded on them, including that the test-integrity guard is a tripwire with no self-anchor and that npm run check can be neutered by its own script.' (a) UNMERGED IS FALSE. All five branches -- WP-0A-A0-002, WP-0A-CON-002, WP-0A-CON-003, WP-0A-CON-004 and WP-0A-CON-005 -- reached main, in pull requests #3 through #7 and later re-merges. The inheritance itself STANDS: all five still read status in_review, so every open blocker recorded on them is still open and still inherited by this package. (b) NEUTERED BY ITS OWN SCRIPT IS ANSWERED ON THE CI PATH ONLY. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `node scripts/verify-test-coverage-floor.mjs` as its own step, 'Verify test-integrity guard', before it runs `npm run check`, per RFC-2026-007 (Approved 2026-09-02). A guard the workflow invokes cannot be short-circuited by the scripts.check string. It is not answered for a local `npm run check`, where the chain still invokes its own guard and a trailing `&` or a chain of `||` still exits 0 having run nothing. (c) NO SELF-ANCHOR IS HALF ANSWERED, AND THE REMAINING HALF STAYS. An outside anchor now exists: branch protection on main has been real since 2026-09-02 -- strict required status check `bootstrap`, enforce_admins true, no force push, no branch deletion -- and it was tested rather than merely configured, a direct push by an admin being rejected with GH006 (evidence/g0-tracker-th.md). What has not changed is that the guard is a TRIPWIRE and not a control: a commit that edits a protected file and updates its digest in the same commit passes, the guard says so in its own exit-86 message, and the integrity manifest is the one unanchored artifact -- nothing inside this repository can verify it. No required pull-request review is configured either, because the Product Owner opens the pull requests and GitHub forbids approving your own, so the human half of the anchor is the Product Owner reading a diff rather than a control. Note for a reader who checks: OVERNIGHT-SUMMARY.md item 3 still describes protected CI as unavailable pending a paid plan. That file contradicts evidence/g0-tracker-th.md and the guard's own message, and it belongs to no package this run may amend.
prefer_cross_vendor_review is not satisfied; see independence.cross_vendor_exception. Recorded as an exception, not waived.
Gate G0 remains Specification Baseline Complete / External Verification Pending; this package is restricted to reversible, synthetic-only work.

SUPERSEDED 2026-09-06 BY MEASUREMENT, not by memory. This entry read: 'The 30% mutation-coverage floor is a floor, not a target. The catalog sits at 42.4% and the weakest contract at 32.4%.' Every number in it is stale. The floor in test-kits/contracts/schema-mutation-coverage.test.mjs is now COVERAGE_FLOOR = 0.70, and its own comment records that when the metric was corrected to count assertion keywords only, the catalog figure the old metric reported as 42.4% was really 19.3% -- the old one counted bare property names as constraint sites. RE-MEASURED AT THIS HEAD: catalog 654 of 721 constraint sites killed by a declared fixture = 90.7%; weakest contract ctr-ntf-001 at 30 of 39 = 76.9%. Method, so it can be repeated: copy test-kits/contracts/schema-mutation-coverage.test.mjs and json-schema-subset.mjs to a scratch directory, change COVERAGE_FLOOR to 1.01 so that every contract is reported rather than only the failing ones, and run `node --test --test-name-pattern="mutation-coverage floor" <copy>` from the repository root; the per-contract killed/total pairs are in the assertion message and the catalog figure is their sum. Nothing in the repository was edited to measure this. WHAT THE ENTRY WAS FOR STILL STANDS: a floor is not a target. 67 constraint sites across the catalog are killed by no fixture at all, and each one is a rule that nothing exercises. A 70% floor against a measured 90.7% leaves twenty points in which coverage can regress with nothing failing; what actually holds the line is the per-contract UNKILLED_CEILING and SITE_FLOOR tables, which are exact and must be edited deliberately. Raising the floor is still cheap and should still be done as coverage rises. One consequence for a reader of this list: the '82% coverage' figure quoted in the next-but-one entry predates this measurement and was left untouched because it was not re-measured.

Roughly 71% of the 441 generated counterexamples are MECHANICAL -- they violate a rule with a sentinel value (`zz not matching pattern`) rather than with a value a producer could plausibly emit. Independent testing measured it and the judgement is accepted: the 66 enum, pattern and format fixtures are the weakest, because those keywords are exactly where a contract encodes a specific hazard and a sentinel erases it. They are load-bearing -- each one is a real witness that kills exactly one site -- but they are not documentation, and 82% coverage should not be read as 82% of the catalog's hazards being illustrated.

SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-09-06 BY MEASUREMENT. This entry read: 'Conditional constraint sites -- the allOf/if/then business rules -- sit at 57.6% against 88.8% for plain leaf assertions.' Both numbers moved. RE-MEASURED AT THIS HEAD, partitioning the same constraint sites with the suite's own CONDITIONAL set and the same `site.some(...)` predicate it uses elsewhere: conditional sites 95 of 146 = 65.1%; plain leaf assertions 559 of 575 = 97.2%. The two halves sum to the 654 of 721 measured for the floor above, which is the cross-check that the partition lost nothing. Method as for the entry above -- a scratch copy of the suite, run with `node --test` from the repository root, nothing in the repository edited. THE FINDING SURVIVES ITS NUMBERS: the conditional half still trails the leaf half by 32 points, and 51 of the 67 sites that no fixture kills are conditional. THE EXPLANATION IS NOT RE-VERIFIED AND IS LEFT AS RECORDED: the claim that the generator's naming scheme drops allOf/then/index segments, that 52 names would therefore have collided, and that it SKIPPED those sites rather than misnaming them, was independent testing's reading of the generator's output. The generator is not in the repository tree, so that claim cannot be re-run here; it stands as testimony, not as something this run measured.
